**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/26 (Fri) 11:13
- [EVENT] A giant aquarium in the lobby of the Radisson Blu in Berlin burst, flooding the hotel and nearby streets.
- [FACT] The aquarium, called AquaDom, contained a million litres of water.
- [FACT] AquaDom was home to 1,500 tropical fish.
- [FACT] The aquarium was 15.85 meters high (52 ft) and was the largest free-standing cylindrical aquarium in the world.
- [EVENT] Two people were injured by falling glass after the aquarium burst.
- [FACT] Police reported "incredible" damage from the incident.
- [EVENT] Video footage showed an empty tank with water pouring into the hotel lobby.
- [EVENT] Guests were moved out of the hotel following the incident at 05:50 (04:50 GMT).
- [FACT] The majority of the fish in the aquarium died, and cold weather made rescue attempts more difficult.
- [FACT] The aquarium contained more than 100 different species of fish.
- [FACT] Debris was found in front of the hotel’s front doors, which were twisted by the force of the explosion.
- [RELATIONSHIP] Paul Maletzki was staying on the fourth floor of the hotel with his girlfriend.
- [EVENT] Paul Maletzki described being woken up by a loud bang and shaking.
- [EVENT] Paul Maletzki saw water flowing across the lobby when he looked down.
- [EVENT] Guests were escorted out of the hotel by armed police.
- [RELATIONSHIP] The Mayor of Berlin, Franziska Giffey, visited the hotel to assess the damage.
- [FACT] The Mayor described the tank burst as being like a tsunami and expressed relief that it happened early in the morning.
- [RELATIONSHIP] Sandra Weeser, a member of the German federal parliament, was staying at the hotel.
- [EVENT] Sandra Weeser described being woken up by "a kind of shock wave."
- [EVENT] Sandra Weeser recalled seeing a "large parrotfish lying on the ground, frozen."
- [FACT] The aquarium was modernized two years ago and had a clear-walled lift for visitors.
- [FACT] Some hotel rooms were advertised as having views of the aquarium.
- [EVENT] More than 100 firefighters were sent to the scene.
- [FACT] It was unclear what caused the aquarium to break.
- [EVENT] Rescue dogs were used to check the area inside the hotel for anyone potentially injured, with nobody found.
- [FACT] Police reported "massive amounts" of water flowing into nearby streets.
- [EVENT] People in the area were advised to drive cautiously.
- [FACT] A police source stated there was no evidence of a targeted attack.
